Two-sided inverse minimum-singular-value inequalities reduce moment existence exactly to that for G, including equality divergence. Gaussian QR/Bartlett diagonal chi laws give exponent ell-(m-r)+1 by necessity from final inverse diagonal and sufficiency from inverse triangular entries. value.rationale: Sketched QR guarantees are generally high-probability while actual reconstructed Euclidean basis diagnostics can have divergent unconditional moments even for perfectly orthonormal input. The rank-sensitive sharp cutoffs give a concrete design boundary: at minimal oversampling rank-zero retained block has infinite expected Gram defect, but rank-one anchored retention rescues finite expectation. This is a structurally motivated threshold for an established block-preserving numerical orthogonalizer, not an arbitrary parameter slice; risks include small nonzero singular values causing large finite constants and no statement on actual finite-precision error.
